stem: A team deploys the same bundle to a dev target and later to a prod target. After the dev deployment the scheduled job never fires on its own, although the job exists and runs fine when started by hand. The team must explain the difference the target's mode made.

option_texts.A: Development mode pauses all schedules and triggers on the deployed resources
option_texts.B: Development mode omits the schedule mapping, so the deployed job carries no schedule
option_texts.C: Development mode marks the job read-only until a production deployment promotes it
option_texts.D: Development mode needs a cluster id, and the schedule waits until one is supplied

drill_answer_short: Deploying a target in development mode pauses all schedules and triggers on deployed resources
decision_hinge: Deploying a target in development mode pauses all schedules and triggers on deployed resources such as jobs, and to unpause an individual job you set the pause_status to UNPAUSED.

plausible_options.C: the scheduled job never fires on its own

eliminated_by.B: the job exists and runs fine when started by hand
eliminated_by.D: The team must explain the difference the target's mode made

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - the schedule is deployed intact and simply left paused
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - the job is editable and runnable, only its triggers are paused
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a cluster id is optional in development mode and unrelated to scheduling

stem: After a dev deployment of a bundle, the team finds the job listed in the workspace under a name that is not the one written in databricks.yml. Nothing in the configuration sets a name override, and the same bundle deployed to prod shows the plain name.

option_texts.A: Development mode appends the target name to every deployed resource name
option_texts.B: Development mode prepends a dev prefix carrying the deploying user's short name
option_texts.C: Development mode renames each resource to its resource key instead of its display name
option_texts.D: The workspace adds the owner to a name whenever two jobs would otherwise collide

drill_answer_short: Development mode prepends [dev <short_name>] to deployed resource names and tags them with a dev tag
decision_hinge: Deploying in development mode prepends all resources that are not deployed as files or notebooks with the prefix dev and the current user short_name, and tags each deployed job and pipeline with a dev Databricks tag.

plausible_options.A: a name that is not the one written in databricks.yml

eliminated_by.C: Nothing in the configuration sets a name override
eliminated_by.D: the same bundle deployed to prod shows the plain name

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the marker is a prepended dev prefix, not an appended target name
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - the resource key is not substituted for the display name
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - the rename comes from the deployment mode, not from collision handling

stem: An engineer has edited several notebooks inside a Databricks Git folder and the folder UI highlights the edits. Those edits now have to reach the remote repository so a colleague can open a pull request against them.

option_texts.A: Re-run a bundle deploy, which writes the notebooks back to the remote repository
option_texts.B: Click Pull in the Git dialog, which synchronises the folder with the remote
option_texts.C: Add a commit message in the Git dialog and click Commit and Push
option_texts.D: Export the notebooks as source files and attach them to the pull request

drill_answer_short: Add a required commit message in the Git folder UI, then Commit & Push to send the changes to the remote
decision_hinge: When you make changes to existing notebooks or files the Git folder UI highlights the changes; you add a required commit message for the changes and click Commit and Push.

plausible_options.B: Those edits now have to reach the remote repository

eliminated_by.A: the folder UI highlights the edits
eliminated_by.D: so a colleague can open a pull request against them

distractor_traps.A: T2: scope error - a bundle deploy sends resources to a workspace, never to a Git remote
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - Pull brings remote commits down, it does not publish local edits
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - a pull request is opened from a pushed branch, not from attached files

stem: A financial services firm has to bring account rows from an on-premises PostgreSQL database into Databricks every night, and wants the ingest to carry across row-level inserts, updates and deletes rather than reload the whole table.

option_texts.A: Use a streaming read on the database table so each change arrives as a micro-batch
option_texts.B: Use Auto Loader against the database, since it discovers new rows the same way it discovers files
option_texts.C: Use COPY INTO against the database endpoint so each night's rows append idempotently
option_texts.D: Use a Lakeflow Connect managed connector, which reads relational databases using change data capture

drill_answer_short: Lakeflow Connect managed connectors ingest from relational databases such as PostgreSQL using change data capture
decision_hinge: Lakeflow Connect managed connectors ingest data from relational databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server using change data capture.

plausible_options.A: wants the ingest to carry across row-level inserts, updates and deletes

eliminated_by.B: bring account rows from an on-premises PostgreSQL database into Databricks
eliminated_by.C: rather than reload the whole table

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a streaming read sounds incremental, but the managed connector is what supplies change data capture
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - Auto Loader discovers files in cloud object storage, not rows in a database
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - COPY INTO loads files from a storage location, not from a database endpoint

stem: An analytics team has to land Salesforce and Workday records in Unity Catalog on a schedule. They would rather not build and operate their own extraction code against either vendor API.

option_texts.A: A custom connector written against each vendor API and run as a notebook task
option_texts.B: A Lakeflow Connect managed connector, which covers enterprise SaaS applications
option_texts.C: An Auto Loader stream pointed at an export folder each vendor writes nightly
option_texts.D: A federated query that reads each vendor system live at report time

drill_answer_short: Managed connectors cover SaaS applications including Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira and Workday
decision_hinge: Managed connectors ingest data from enterprise SaaS applications including Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira, and Workday, and community or custom connectors exist for sources without a built-in option.

plausible_options.C: land Salesforce and Workday records in Unity Catalog on a schedule

eliminated_by.A: would rather not build and operate their own extraction code
eliminated_by.D: records in Unity Catalog on a schedule

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the team explicitly does not want to own extraction code
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - that works only if the vendors already export files, which is extra operating burden
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - federation queries in place rather than landing records on a schedule

stem: An engineer tries to put an 8 GB archive into a Unity Catalog volume using the Add data page in the workspace, and the upload is refused. The same volume already holds much smaller files that arrived the same way.

option_texts.A: The archive format is unsupported, because the upload page accepts only structured data files
option_texts.B: Volumes cap any single file at 5 GB regardless of how the file is written
option_texts.C: The upload UI caps a single file at 5 GB, so a larger file needs another route
option_texts.D: The volume is managed, and managed volumes reject files above a fixed size

drill_answer_short: Uploading through the UI is limited to 5 GB per file; larger files must use a different upload route
decision_hinge: You can upload files of any format to a volume, but when you upload files to a volume through the UI there is a 5 GB file size limit, and to upload files larger than 5 GB you use another method.

eliminated_by.A: tries to put an 8 GB archive into a Unity Catalog volume
eliminated_by.D: already holds much smaller files that arrived the same way

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - a volume accepts structured, semi-structured and unstructured files alike
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - the 5 GB ceiling belongs to the UI path, not to volumes themselves
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no size rule distinguishes managed volumes from others

stem: A team is standing up a managed ingestion pipeline and must decide where the source endpoint and its authentication details belong. Nothing secret may sit in the pipeline configuration that the team commits to source control.

option_texts.A: In a notebook widget where the operator types the authentication details each run
option_texts.B: In the pipeline configuration, encrypted so the committed file reveals nothing
option_texts.C: In a cluster environment variable holding the endpoint, read when the pipeline starts
option_texts.D: In a connection, a securable object holding the endpoint and authentication credentials

drill_answer_short: A connection is the securable object that stores the source endpoint and credentials, so the pipeline config holds none
decision_hinge: A connection is a securable object that stores the source endpoint and authentication credentials for your source, and the managed connector uses this connection to authenticate without requiring credentials in your pipeline configuration.

plausible_options.C: must decide where the source endpoint and its authentication details belong

eliminated_by.A: standing up a managed ingestion pipeline
eliminated_by.B: Nothing secret may sit in the pipeline configuration

distractor_traps.A: T2: scope error - a managed pipeline runs on a schedule with no operator to type a value
distractor_traps.B: T4: breaks a stated requirement - the secret still travels in the committed configuration
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - an environment variable keeps it out of the file but outside Unity Catalog governance
